summary: SSE resume drops final rich attachment (base64 image) and emits heartbeat-only trailer after edge WAF probe
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports that long SSE streams containing a final rich attachment (base64-embedded image) are truncated on reconnect. After a midstream Azure WAF idle probe, the resumed stream returns a small heartbeat-only trailer and the expected base64 image chunk never arrives.

Impact: FinSolutions sees corrupted/wrapped chat transcripts where the final image URL or base64 block is missing. This breaks downstream UX and automated document ingestion. Affects a handful of production requests (estimated ~0.3% of long streaming sessions) in us-east. Customer is enterprise, high priority.

Environment: prod us-east, hosted Redwood API, model pinned to redwood-open-13B-v1, requests originate via customer VPC-to-Redwood edge through Azure WAF/ALB chain.

Steps to reproduce (customer-supplied):
1) Start a long chat request that ends with an instruction to attach an image as base64 and a short concluding paragraph. The full server stream normally emits text tokens then an "attachment" choice containing the base64 payload.
2) Midway through token emission perform a simulated Azure WAF idle probe (customer does this regularly from their edge).
3) Client reconnects/resumes SSE using the session resume token.

Observed behavior: After resume the client receives:
- resumption ACK, a few text tokens repeating a short prefix, then a single keepalive/heartbeat line ("event: heartbeat" + tiny payload), and then connection close. The large base64 attachment is not delivered. The server logs show the final choice was generated and committed but downstream connection to the WAF/edge was closed before the attachment chunk was flushed to the client.

Expected behavior: On resume the remaining tokens including the final attachment should be delivered intact, or a clear error/rollback should be returned. Heartbeat-only trailers should not suppress pending payload frames.

Notes: This appears distinct from earlier "fragment duplication" cases — here the issue is loss of a large trailing chunk (attachment) combined with a synthetic keepalive from the edge. Customer indicates their edge probe pattern differs from standard health checks; the probe performs a lightweight HEAD/GET that can cause the connection to briefly half-close and trigger downstream buffering behaviors.

investigation_notes: Traces: request_id 7f9d3c (customer example) shows model generation finished; final chunk appended to outgoing stream buffer at 14:01:32.389Z.

Edge event: Azure WAF inserted a synthetic probe and subsequently returned 200 to the probe; logs show a half-close from the WAF side at 14:01:33.041Z which aligns with missing attachment delivery window.

Runtime behavior: sendQueue.flush() called but heartbeat emission path runs concurrently; race condition observed where small heartbeat frame is written after sendQueue flush flags cleared, but large chunk remained in overflow buffer guarded by 'resumeLocked' flag and was skipped on resume.

Staging repro: toggling the probe to occur after final flush avoids the loss. Repro rate in staging ~70% when probe placed between final token emission and stream termination; implies timing-sensitive race.

Potential root cause: ordering/race in resume path between flush/commit of large payload frames and keepalive/heartbeat generation when an upstream/edge emits an out-of-band connection probe causing half-close semantics.
Relevant code area: streaming reconstructor and sse-session manager (v2.7.1). Candidate fix ensures flushLargeFrames() is awaited before emitting heartbeat or returning resume READY to client.
next_steps: Finish internal PR review and run extended streaming regression suite against stagers with simulated edge probes.
Create a short-term mitigation for customer: feature-flag to disable midstream keepalive emission for resumed sessions or maintain a forced flush-on-resume behavior.
Canary deploy fix to prod us-east in a low-traffic window, monitor token delivery and SLOs for streaming.
Coordinate with customer FinSolutions to temporarily suppress edge probes or whitelist streaming endpoints while canary runs.
Postmortem/Follow-up: add synthetic probe test cases to CI and update runbook for WAF/edge interactions.
workarounds: Customer workaround: avoid injecting idle probes during active long streams; increase edge probe interval for identified endpoints. Temporary support flag provided to customer to enable forced flush-on-resume while fix is rolled out.
notes: This ticket differs from standard fragmented-chunk issues because the missing payload is a large base64 attachment combined with an external edge probe. Add E2E tests that simulate probe-caused half-close semantics (HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2).
